body: Two assumptions quietly assume away the hardest problems in this design, and one of them is factually wrong. First, the eBird Basic Dataset is not downloadable 'without authentication issues' — EBD access requires a signed data-use agreement with the Cornell Lab, so the P1 pipeline's core input is gated behind a license step the spec never plans for. Second, the data-quality assumption waves off exactly the confound that citizen-science phenology studies live or die by: observer effort in eBird varies enormously across space, season, and year (more checklists on weekends, in spring, near cities), and 'first arrival' metrics are especially sensitive to effort — a later first-arrival date can simply mean fewer observers. The spec's aggregation (FR-002) counts raw observations per grid cell with no effort normalization (checklists per unit effort, or an occupancy/detection model), so the phenology-climate correlation risks measuring observer behavior rather than bird behavior. This is not a peripheral caveat; it is the difference between a climate-sensitivity estimate and an artifact. Additionally, the many [deferred] thresholds (SC-002 through SC-004, acceptance scenario 1) leave the success criteria currently unmeasurable — the spec asserts targets it has not set.
